speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with the basics: can you describe exactly where you feel the pain, and does it radiate to your arm, jaw, or back? Also, have you noticed any sweating, nausea, or dizziness accompanying this?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain feels like a tight squeezing right in the center of my chest, and it shoots out to my jaw and left arm. When it gets bad, I break out in a cold sweat and feel out of breath, but I haven't felt any nausea. It mostly happens when I'm trying to work hard or move quickly. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Coronary Syndrome (Suspected Myocardial Infarction). Given the classic presentation of squeezing chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm, accompanied by diaphoresis and triggered by exertion, immediate cardiology evaluation and ECG are critical.
